_comment: Your Working Desktop. Add an entry per app; the page shows one card each. `command` is run through the shell, so quoting/&& work as they do in Terminal. `cwd` accepts ~. `probe` is how the page tells whether the app is already running -- port for web apps, process for GUI ones. Add `"type": "action"` for a one-shot command instead: no probe, no Stop, just Run and the result. Only ids listed here can ever be launched; the browser never sends a command.

apps.name: 一目弈镜 · Go Review
apps.note: KataGo review dashboard for your Fox / LizzieYZY games.

apps.name: Neo · English Adventure
apps.note: Colourful English playground for a 6-year-old: flashcards, listening, speaking, phonics, stories and rhymes.

apps.name: Kick Cloudflare Tunnel
apps.note: Force cloudflared to reconnect now instead of waiting out its backoff. Use when my-english-coach.com shows Error 1033.
apps._sudo_note: kickstart needs root, and there is no terminal here to type a password into -- osascript asks macOS for the authorisation dialog instead, so no password is ever stored or passed on a command line.
apps.command: osascript -e 'do shell script "launchctl kickstart -k system/com.cloudflare.cloudflared" with administrator privileges'

apps.name: LizzieYZY
apps.note: KataGo GUI for analysing a game move by move.
apps._cwd_note: Lizzie reads config.txt / persist from its working directory. ~ matches running the command from a fresh Terminal, which is where your current engine settings live -- changing this points Lizzie at a different config.
